09-01.t: Birth of Carl Gunnar Engström, Inventor of the Engström Respirator
09-01.s: Swedish physician and engineer Carl Gunnar Engström was born; he later invented the Engström volume-controlled respirator in 1953, advancing mechanical ventilation in intensive care and anesthesia.

09-01.t: Launch of National Nutrition Week in India
09-01.s: The Food and Nutrition Board initiated India's annual National Nutrition Week (September 1-7) to raise public awareness about balanced diets, micronutrients, and combating malnutrition.

09-01.t: Over 170 Nations Join WHO-Led COVAX Facility
09-01.s: More than 170 countries signed on to the COVID-19 Vaccine Global Access Facility (COVAX), a global initiative spearheaded by the World Health Organization to develop and equitably distribute COVID-19 vaccines worldwide.

09-02.t: Birth of Allen Oldfather Whipple, Pioneer of Pancreatic Surgery
09-02.s: American surgeon Allen Oldfather Whipple was born; he later described pancreaticoduodenectomy (the Whipple procedure) in 1935 and Whipple's triad for insulinoma in 1938.

09-02.t: Death of Maude Abbott, Pioneer of Congenital Heart Disease
09-02.s: Canadian physician Maude Elizabeth Seymour Abbott died; she was a leading authority on congenital heart disease and described Rokitansky-Maude Abbott syndrome.

09-03.t: Alexander Fleming Returns to Discover Penicillin Mold
09-03.s: Returning from holiday at St. Mary's Hospital in London, Scottish bacteriologist Alexander Fleming noticed a Penicillium mold inhibiting Staphylococcus colonies on a petri dish, leading to the discovery of penicillin.

09-03.t: WHO Recommends Corticosteroids for Severe COVID-19
09-03.s: The World Health Organization and JAMA issued recommendations supporting systemic corticosteroids such as dexamethasone for severe COVID-19 after clinical studies showed significant mortality reduction.

09-04.t: Birth of Edgar Alexander Pask, Resuscitation and Anesthesia Pioneer
09-04.s: English anesthetist Edgar 'Gar' Alexander Pask was born; he conducted landmark self-experimentation on artificial respiration, hypothermia prevention, and life-jacket safety.

09-04.t: FDA Approves Bosutinib for Chronic Myelogenous Leukemia
09-04.s: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved bosutinib (Bosulif), a tyrosine kinase inhibitor developed for the treatment of chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML).

09-05.t: Birth of Rudolf Nissen, Pioneer of Fundoplication
09-05.s: German surgeon Rudolf Nissen was born; he later developed the Nissen fundoplication surgical procedure for gastroesophageal reflux disease.

09-05.t: Death of Rudolf Virchow, Father of Modern Pathology
09-05.s: German physician and pathologist Rudolf Virchow died in Berlin; he established cellular pathology ('Omnis cellula e cellula'), modernized autopsy technique, and championed social medicine.

09-05.t: Birth of Dr. K. K. Aggarwal
09-05.s: Cardiologist, Padma Shri awardee, and former National President of the Indian Medical Association Dr. Krishan Kumar Aggarwal was born in New Delhi.

09-06.t: Birth of Marie Elisabeth Zakrzewska, Hospital Founder
09-06.s: Prussian-born physician Marie Elisabeth Zakrzewska was born; she founded the New England Hospital for Women and Children, expanding clinical care and medical training for women.

09-06.t: Birth of John J. R. Macleod, Co-Discoverer of Insulin
09-06.s: Scottish biochemist and physiologist John James Rickard Macleod was born; he shared the 1923 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery of insulin.

09-06.t: DCGI Approves Bharat Biotech's iNCOVACC Intranasal COVID-19 Vaccine
09-06.s: The Drugs Controller General of India approved Bharat Biotech's iNCOVACC (BBV154) for restricted emergency use in adults, making it the world's first intranasal COVID-19 vaccine to receive regulatory approval.

09-07.t: Birth of Michael E. DeBakey, Pioneer of Cardiovascular Surgery
09-07.s: American cardiac surgeon and medical innovator Michael Ellis DeBakey was born; he pioneered aortic aneurysm repair, coronary bypass procedures, and the Mobile Army Surgical Hospital (MASH) concept.

09-07.t: Death of William Stewart Halsted, Father of Modern Surgery
09-07.s: American surgeon William Stewart Halsted died; he introduced surgical rubber gloves, aseptic technique, radical mastectomy, and the modern surgical residency training model.

09-07.t: Passing of Dr. Chintaman Govind Pandit
09-07.s: Dr. C. G. Pandit, founding Director of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and Padma Bhushan awardee, passed away at age 96.

09-08.t: Death of Hermann von Helmholtz, Inventor of the Ophthalmoscope
09-08.s: German physician and physicist Hermann von Helmholtz died; he invented the ophthalmoscope in 1850 and formulated the Young-Helmholtz trichromatic theory of color vision.

09-08.t: Death of John Franklin Enders, Poliovirus Culture Pioneer
09-08.s: American microbiologist John Franklin Enders died; he shared the 1954 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for culturing poliovirus in non-neural tissue, enabling the development of polio and measles vaccines.

09-09.t: Ludwig Rehn Performs First Successful Suture of a Human Heart
09-09.s: German surgeon Ludwig Rehn successfully sutured a right ventricular stab wound in a 22-year-old patient in Frankfurt, inaugurating the modern era of cardiac surgery.

09-09.t: World Federation of Societies of Anaesthesiologists Founded
09-09.s: The World Federation of Societies of Anaesthesiologists (WFSA) was founded at the first World Congress of Anaesthesiologists in Scheveningen, Netherlands, to advance global anesthesia and resuscitation standards.

09-09.t: Launch of Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
09-09.s: President Droupadi Murmu virtually launched the Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan to mobilize community and corporate nutritional support (Ni-kshay Mitra) toward India's tuberculosis elimination goals.

09-10.t: Birth of Thomas Sydenham, 'The English Hippocrates'
09-10.s: English physician Thomas Sydenham was born; he authored Observationes Medicae and provided classic clinical descriptions of gout, scarlet fever, and Sydenham's chorea.

09-10.t: Birth of Marthe Gautier, Co-Discoverer of Trisomy 21
09-10.s: French pediatric cardiologist and researcher Marthe Gautier was born; she played a pivotal role in identifying the extra chromosome 21 responsible for Down syndrome.

09-11.t: Birth of Joseph Gustav Asherman, Describer of Asherman Syndrome
09-11.s: Obstetrician and gynecologist Joseph Gustav Asherman was born; he described intrauterine adhesions and amenorrhea following uterine trauma (Asherman syndrome) in 1948.

09-11.t: Death of Ivor Lewis, Pioneer of Esophageal Surgery
09-11.s: Welsh surgeon Ivor Lewis died; he introduced the two-stage Ivor Lewis esophagectomy in 1946 for the surgical resection of esophageal carcinoma.

09-12.t: Birth of Rudolph Matas, Father of Vascular Surgery
09-12.s: American surgeon Rudolph Matas was born; he pioneered endoaneurysmorrhaphy and spinal anesthesia techniques, earning recognition as the father of vascular surgery.

09-12.t: First Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Performed by Erich Mühe
09-12.s: German surgeon Prof. Dr. med. Erich Mühe performed the world's first laparoscopic cholecystectomy in Böblingen, Germany, launching the era of minimally invasive abdominal surgery.

09-13.t: Phineas Gage Survives Severe Frontal Lobe Tamping Iron Injury
09-13.s: Railroad foreman Phineas Gage survived an explosion that drove an iron rod through his skull and left frontal lobe, becoming a landmark case in understanding brain localization and personality.

09-13.t: Birth of Walter Reed, Yellow Fever Researcher
09-13.s: U.S. Army physician Walter Reed was born; in 1901 he led the team that confirmed Carlos Finlay's theory that yellow fever is transmitted by mosquitoes.

09-13.t: India's Second Human Heart Transplant Performed by Dr. P. K. Sen
09-13.s: Cardiothoracic surgeon Dr. P. K. Sen performed India's second human heart transplant at KEM Hospital in Bombay, though the recipient succumbed to pulmonary hypertension 14 hours post-operatively.
President Droupadi Murmu virtually launched the nationwide Ayushman Bhav campaign from Gandhinagar to achieve saturation coverage of Ayushman cards, ABHA IDs, and community health screenings.

09-14.t: Birth of Ferid Murad, Nitric Oxide Signaling Nobel Laureate
09-14.s: American physician and pharmacologist Ferid Murad was born; he shared the 1998 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering that nitroglycerin acts by releasing nitric oxide to relax smooth muscle.

09-14.t: First Approved Human Gene Therapy Trial Begins
09-14.s: Four-year-old Ashanti DeSilva, who had ADA-SCID, received genetically modified T cells at the NIH in the world's first approved human gene therapy clinical trial.

09-15.t: First Public Presentation of Local Anesthesia Using Cocaine
09-15.s: At the German Ophthalmological Society congress in Heidelberg, Josef Brettauer presented Carl Koller's experiments demonstrating cocaine's efficacy as a topical local anesthetic for eye surgery.

09-15.t: Birth of Luther Terry, U.S. Surgeon General Who Warned on Tobacco
09-15.s: American physician Luther Terry was born; as the ninth U.S. Surgeon General, he issued the landmark 1964 report linking cigarette smoking to lung cancer and heart disease.

09-16.t: Birth of Albrecht Kossel, Nucleic Acid Nobel Laureate
09-16.s: German biochemist Albrecht Kossel was born; he won the 1910 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for determining the chemical composition of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).

09-16.t: Death of Sir Thomas Lauder Brunton, Nitrate Therapy Pioneer
09-16.s: Scottish physician Sir Thomas Lauder Brunton died; he introduced amyl nitrite in 1867 for the relief of angina pectoris, laying the foundation for nitrate therapy in cardiology.

09-17.t: Death of Henrik Sjögren, Describer of Sjögren Syndrome
09-17.s: Swedish ophthalmologist Henrik Samuel Conrad Sjögren died; he described keratoconjunctivitis sicca (Sjögren syndrome) and introduced 1% rose bengal staining in 1933.

09-17.t: Inaugural WHO World Patient Safety Day
09-17.s: Following its adoption by the World Health Assembly in 2019, the World Health Organization established September 17 as World Patient Safety Day to reduce preventable harm in healthcare.

09-17.t: India Sets Single-Day Record of 2.5 Crore COVID-19 Vaccine Doses
09-17.s: India's national COVID-19 immunization program achieved its highest single-day vaccination total, administering 2.5 crore doses in 24 hours.

09-18.t: Birth of Uğur Şahin, Co-Developer of mRNA COVID-19 Vaccine
09-18.s: German immunologist and BioNTech co-founder Uğur Şahin was born; his research led to the first authorized mRNA-based vaccine for COVID-19.

09-18.t: Inauguration of Apollo Hospitals in Chennai
09-18.s: Founded by cardiologist Dr. Prathap C. Reddy, Apollo Hospitals opened in Chennai as India's first corporate hospital, ushering in private tertiary and quaternary healthcare infrastructure across the country.
Surgeons at the University of Gothenburg in Sweden performed the world's first mother-to-daughter uterus transplantation, advancing reproductive transplant surgery.

09-19.t: James Leonard Corning Publishes Regional Anesthesia Technique
09-19.s: American neurologist James Leonard Corning published an experimental method in the New York Medical Journal to prolong regional anesthesia by restricting blood flow to prolong cocaine's neural action.

09-19.t: Birth of Irving Freiler Stein, Co-Describer of PCOS
09-19.s: American gynecologist Irving Freiler Stein was born; he co-described Stein-Leventhal syndrome, now known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), in 1934.

09-20.t: Luigi Galvani Records Pivotal 'Animal Electricity' Observation
09-20.s: Italian physician and anatomist Luigi Galvani observed a dissected frog's leg muscle contract when its nerve was touched by a metal scalpel near an electrical machine, founding electrophysiology.

09-20.t: Death of Ernest William Goodpasture, Pathologist
09-20.s: American pathologist Ernest William Goodpasture died; he described Goodpasture syndrome in 1919 and pioneered viral cultivation in chick embryos for vaccine production.

09-21.t: Birth of Charles Nicolle, Discoverer of Typhus Transmission
09-21.s: French bacteriologist Charles Nicolle was born; he won the 1928 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering that body lice transmit epidemic typhus.

09-21.t: Death of Fidel Pagés, Pioneer of Epidural Anesthesia
09-21.s: Spanish military surgeon Fidel Pagés Miravé died; his landmark 1921 paper introduced 'anestesia metamérica,' the first clinical description of lumbar epidural anesthesia.

09-22.t: Birth of Dorothy Reed Mendenhall, Co-Describer of Reed-Sternberg Cells
09-22.s: American physician Dorothy Reed was born; in 1902 she characterized the giant multinucleated cells (Reed-Sternberg cells) diagnostic of Hodgkin lymphoma.

09-22.t: Birth of John W. Lachman, Developer of the Lachman Test
09-22.s: American orthopedic surgeon John W. Lachman was born; he devised the Lachman test (1976), the gold-standard physical exam maneuver for anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.

09-23.t: Death of Hermann Boerhaave, Pioneer of Clinical Teaching
09-23.s: Dutch physician Hermann Boerhaave died; he pioneered bedside clinical instruction in Leiden and first described spontaneous esophageal rupture (Boerhaave syndrome) in 1724.

09-23.t: Josef Jadassohn Presents Patch Testing for Contact Dermatitis
09-23.s: German dermatologist Josef Jadassohn presented his findings on eczematous skin reactions to mercurial compounds at the 5th Congress of the German Society of Dermatology, establishing diagnostic patch testing.

Organic chemist and phytomedicine pioneer Dr. Asima Chatterjee was born in Calcutta; she became the first woman to earn a D.Sc. from an Indian university and developed the anti-epileptic drug Ayush-56 alongside research on vinca alkaloids and anti-malarials.

09-23.t: Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose Takes Oath as India's First Woman Legislator
09-23.s: Physician and Acting Surgeon General of Travancore Dr. Mary Poonen Lukose took oath as a member of the Travancore Legislative Council, becoming India's first female legislator while championing public health reforms.

09-23.t: Launch of Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)
09-23.s: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched AB-PMJAY in Ranchi, Jharkhand, establishing one of the world's largest government-funded health assurance schemes for secondary and tertiary hospitalization.

09-24.t: Birth of Jerome W. Conn, Describer of Conn Syndrome
09-24.s: American endocrinologist Jerome W. Conn was born; in 1955 he described primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome) and helped elucidate the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis.

09-24.t: Birth of Dr. Autar Singh Paintal
09-24.s: Indian physiologist Dr. Autar Singh Paintal was born in Mogok; he discovered pulmonary J-receptors and became the first Indian physiologist elected Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS), later serving as DG of ICMR.

09-24.t: Death of André Frédéric Cournand, Cardiac Catheterization Nobel Laureate
09-24.s: French-born American physician André Frédéric Cournand died; he shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing cardiac catheterization.

09-24.t: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021 Enforced
09-24.s: Notified in the Gazette of India, the MTP Amendment Act, 2021 came into force, extending the upper gestation limit for abortion to 24 weeks for special categories and expanding access to unmarried women.

09-25.t: Death of Carl Wunderlich, Pioneer of Clinical Thermometry
09-25.s: German physician Carl Reinhold August Wunderlich died; his 1868 treatise established 37 °C (98.6 °F) as normal human body temperature and introduced routine clinical thermometry.
Dr. Rukhmabai, colonial India's second qualified and practicing woman physician and a landmark figure in social reform leading to the Age of Consent Act, passed away in Bombay at age 90.

09-25.t: Death of Werner Forssmann, Pioneer of Cardiac Catheterization
09-25.s: German physician Werner Forssmann died; in 1929 he performed the first human cardiac catheterization on himself, earning a share of the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

09-25.t: National Medical Commission (NMC) Replaces Medical Council of India
09-25.s: The National Medical Commission formally came into force, repealing the Indian Medical Council Act, 1956 and dissolving the Medical Council of India as the apex regulator of medical education and practice.

09-26.t: Birth of Ivan Pavlov, Pioneer of Classical Conditioning
09-26.s: Russian physiologist Ivan Pavlov was born; he won the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his research on digestive physiology and classical conditioning.

09-26.t: Birth of Ugo Cerletti, Co-Developer of Electroconvulsive Therapy
09-26.s: Italian neuropsychiatrist Ugo Cerletti was born; in 1938 he and Lucio Bini introduced electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) for severe psychiatric disorders.

09-27.t: Mary Toft Medical Hoax Investigation Begins
09-27.s: Mary Toft of Surrey, England, was reported to have delivered animal parts, prompting an investigation by leading London physicians including obstetrician James Douglas, who exposed the fraud.

09-27.t: Measles Certified Eliminated from the Americas
09-27.s: The Pan American Health Organization and World Health Organization certified the Region of the Americas free of endemic measles, marking a historic vaccination milestone.

09-27.t: National Rollout of Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)
09-27.s: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the nationwide rollout of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission via video conference to build India's interoperable digital health infrastructure and ABHA health accounts.

09-28.t: Death of Louis Pasteur, Father of Microbiology and Immunology
09-28.s: French chemist and microbiologist Louis Pasteur died; his discoveries of germ theory, pasteurization, and vaccines against anthrax and rabies transformed medicine. World Rabies Day is observed on this date.
Scottish bacteriologist Alexander Fleming observed that a Penicillium mold contaminating a Staphylococcus culture plate lysed surrounding bacteria, ushering in the antibiotic era.

09-28.t: Passing of Dr. M. S. Swaminathan
09-28.s: Geneticist and architect of India's Green Revolution Dr. M. S. Swaminathan, whose work eradicated chronic famine and reshaped nutritional security in India, passed away at age 98.

09-29.t: Birth of François Dessertenne, Describer of Torsades de Pointes
09-29.s: French cardiologist François Dessertenne was born; in 1966 he first described and named the polymorphic ventricular tachycardia known as torsades de pointes.

09-29.t: Death of Willem Einthoven, Inventor of the Electrocardiogram
09-29.s: Dutch physician and physiologist Willem Einthoven died; he developed the first practical string galvanometer electrocardiogram (ECG) in 1903 and won the 1924 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

09-29.t: Supreme Court Affirms Equal Abortion Rights Regardless of Marital Status
09-29.s: In X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Govt. of NCT of Delhi, a three-judge bench of the Supreme Court of India ruled that all women, married or unmarried, have the right to safe and legal abortion up to 24 weeks.

09-30.t: Birth of Barry Marshall, Co-Discoverer of Helicobacter pylori
09-30.s: Australian physician Barry J. Marshall was born; he and Robin Warren proved that Helicobacter pylori causes most peptic ulcers, earning the 2005 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

09-30.t: Death of Robert Arden Miller, Designer of the Miller Laryngoscope Blade
09-30.s: American anesthesiologist Robert Arden Miller died; in 1941 he designed the straight Miller laryngoscope blade, which remains a standard tool for endotracheal intubation.
